title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
description:
Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`, return the `k`-th largest element in the array.

Note that it is the `k`-th largest element in the sorted order, not the `k`-th distinct element.

examples.explanation: The 2nd largest element in sorted order [1,2,3,4,5,6] is 5.

hints: Maintain a min-heap of size k as you iterate through the array.
If the heap size exceeds k, pop the minimum element.
After iterating through all elements, the top of the min-heap is the kth largest element.

solutions.explanation: Use a Min-Heap of capacity k. Insert each element into the heap. When the heap size exceeds k, remove the smallest element. The remaining top element is the kth largest.

dryRunSteps.explanation: Iterate num = 3 and num = 2. Push into min-heap. Size = 2 (matches k = 2).
Push num = 1. Heap is [1, 3, 2]. Size exceeds k (3 > 2), pop minimum root (1). Heap becomes [2, 3].
Push num = 5. Heap is [2, 3, 5]. Size exceeds k (3 > 2), pop minimum root (2). Heap becomes [3, 5].
Push num = 6. Heap is [3, 5, 6]. Size exceeds k, pop minimum root (3). Heap becomes [5, 6].
Push num = 4. Heap is [4, 6, 5]. Size exceeds k, pop minimum root (4). Heap remains [5, 6].
All numbers processed. The top of the min-heap (heap[0]) is 5, the 2nd largest element.

realWorldUseCases.description: Streaming billions of tweets and maintaining top K hashtags using a bounded min-heap.
